title: Grammar: Verb Focus: Ir and Venir
description: 'To go' vs 'to come': irregular forms, al/a la contractions, and choosing between them.

sentences.spanish: Voy al gimnasio tres días por semana.
sentences.english: I go to the gym three days a week.

sentences.spanish: Voy al trabajo en metro.
sentences.english: I go to work by metro.

sentences.spanish: ¿Vas a la fiesta de Marta?
sentences.english: Are you going to Marta's party?

sentences.spanish: Vamos al cine esta noche.
sentences.english: We're going to the cinema tonight.

sentences.spanish: Los niños van al colegio en bici.
sentences.english: The kids go to school by bike.

sentences.spanish: ¿Vais a la playa este fin de semana?
sentences.english: Are you all going to the beach this weekend?

sentences.spanish: Mis padres van al médico cada mes.
sentences.english: My parents go to the doctor every month.

sentences.spanish: Voy a casa de Ana a estudiar.
sentences.english: I'm going over to Ana's place to study.

sentences.spanish: Mañana vamos a ir a Segovia en tren.
sentences.english: Tomorrow we're going to go to Segovia by train.

sentences.spanish: Esta tarde voy a ir al dentista.
sentences.english: This afternoon I'm going to go to the dentist.

sentences.spanish: ¿Adónde vas tan deprisa?
sentences.english: Where are you off to in such a hurry?

sentences.spanish: Vengo enseguida.
sentences.english: I'll be right back.

sentences.spanish: ¿De dónde vienes?
sentences.english: Where are you coming from?

sentences.spanish: Vengo de la oficina.
sentences.english: I'm coming from the office.

sentences.spanish: Mi hermana viene a cenar esta noche.
sentences.english: My sister is coming for dinner tonight.

sentences.spanish: Venimos del mercado con las bolsas llenas.
sentences.english: We're coming back from the market with our bags full.

sentences.spanish: ¿Venís con nosotros al concierto?
sentences.english: Are you all coming with us to the concert?

sentences.spanish: Mis primos vienen de visita este fin de semana.
sentences.english: My cousins are coming to visit this weekend.

sentences.spanish: Yo voy a tu casa; tú vienes a la mía.
sentences.english: I'll go to your house; you come to mine.

sentences.spanish: ¿Puedo venir contigo?
sentences.english: Can I come with you?

sentences.spanish: ¿Cómo vais al trabajo, en coche o andando?
sentences.english: How do you all get to work, by car or walking?

sentences.spanish: Vamos a pie, está al lado.
sentences.english: Let's walk, it's just next door.

sentences.spanish: Todos los veranos vamos a la misma cala.
sentences.english: Every summer we go to the same cove.

sentences.spanish: ¿Vienes al gimnasio hoy?
sentences.english: Are you coming to the gym today?

sentences.spanish: Un día tienes que venir a mi pueblo.
sentences.english: One day you have to come to my village.

sentences.spanish: ¡Hasta luego, me voy corriendo!
sentences.english: See you later, I'm dashing off!

grammarExplanation:
'Ir' = to go (movement AWAY from where the speaker is). 'Venir' = to come (movement TOWARD the speaker or listener).

Ir (irregular):
• Voy = I go • Vas = you go • Va = he/she goes
• Vamos = we go • Vais = you all go • Van = they go

Venir (also irregular):
• Vengo = I come • Vienes • Viene • Venimos • Venís • Vienen

Remember:
• a + el = al → Voy AL gimnasio
• de + el = del → Vengo DEL mercado
• ir + a + infinitive = going to do something → Mañana vamos a ir a Segovia.
